dm: The Perfection of Diligence
gm: Chapter Seven: Teaching Joyous Effort

dm: Thus, with patience, one should initiate diligence, For enlightenment dwells in those who strive in this way. Just as there is no movement without wind, Merit does not arise without diligence.
gm: Thus, having patience, I should undertake diligence. For enlightenment abides in diligence. Just as there is no movement without wind, Merit does not arise without diligence.

dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.

dm: Through savoring the taste of idle pleasure, And the craving that relies on sleep, One does not feel weariness for the suffering of cyclic existence; From these, laziness fully arises.
gm: Tasting the pleasure of idleness, and Craving that relies on sleep; From feeling no weariness toward the sufferings of saṃsāra, Laziness comes to arise.

dm: Having been caught by the hunters of the afflictions, And having entered the snare of rebirth, You have walked into the jaws of the Lord of Death; How can you still not realize this?
gm: Having been snared by the fowler of afflictions, Having entered the net of birth, And having gone into the mouth of the Lord of Death, How is it that you still do not know?

dm: Have you not seen your own kind Being killed one by one? Yet you still rely on sleep, Like a buffalo in the hands of a butcher.
gm: That your own group is gradually being killed, Have you not seen it? Yet whoever relies on sleep, Is like an outcast and a buffalo.

dm: With all paths of escape completely blocked, And while the Lord of Death is watching you, How can you take pleasure in eating, And how can you find such joy in sleeping?
gm: When all paths are blocked, And the Lord of Death is watching, How can you enjoy eating, And how can you enjoy sleeping like this?

dm: Since death will come very quickly, For as long as you can, gather the accumulations. Even if you abandon laziness at that time, What can you do when it is no longer the right time?
gm: Because death will come very quickly, Until then, the accumulations should be gathered. Even if laziness is abandoned at that time, Being out of time, what can be done?

dm: While thinking, "This is not yet done," And "This is only half-finished," The Lord of Death suddenly arrives; "Alas! I am destroyed!" you will think.
gm: "This is undone, this is just begun, And this remains only half-done"— When the Lord of Death suddenly arrives, One will think, "Alas, I am ruined!"

dm: With eyes red and swollen from the force of grief, Tears will stream down your face; As your relatives lose all hope, You will gaze upon the faces of the messengers of the Lord of Death.
gm: Swollen by the force of sorrow, Red eyes shedding tears upon their faces, Relatives having lost hope, And looking at the faces of Yama's messengers.

dm: Tormented by the memory of your own sins, And hearing the sounds of the hells, You will soil your body in terror; When you have become thus delirious, what will you do?
gm: Tormented by the memory of one's own evils, And hearing the sounds of hell, Clothed in excrement out of terror, When one becomes delirious, what can be done?

dm: If you are possessed by such fear in this life, Like a live fish writhing on the ground, What need is there to mention the unbearable Sufferings of hell resulting from your sinful deeds?
gm: If you are fearful in this life, Like a live fish rolling about, Having committed evils, what need is there to mention The unbearable sufferings of hell?

dm: When touched by even warm water, Your tender flesh is intensely scalded; Having committed the actions that lead to hell, How can you remain so at ease?
gm: When touched by hot water, The tender-fleshed find it extremely hot. Having committed the deeds of hell, Why do you remain comfortably like this?

dm: Desiring results without exertion, And being thin-skinned, you are beset by many harms; Though seized by death, you act like an immortal; Alas, you are destroyed by your own sufferings!
gm: Desiring the result without exerting effort, Being fragile and experiencing many harms, Yet acting like a god while seized by death— Alas, you will be destroyed by sufferings!

dm: Relying upon this boat of a human form, Cross over the great river of suffering; Since this boat will be difficult to find again later, O foolish one, do not sleep at such a time!
gm: Relying on the boat of a human body, Free yourself from the great river of suffering. Since this boat will be hard to find later, Fool, do not sleep at this time!

dm: Having abandoned the supreme joy of the sublime Dharma, Which is a boundless cause of delight, Why do you delight in distractions, Frivolity, and the like, which are the causes of suffering?
gm: Which is a boundless cause of joy, Having abandoned the supreme joy of the holy Dharma, In distraction by the causes of suffering, And in frivolity and the like, why do you delight?

dm: Without despondency, with an army of forces, With earnest application and self-mastery, Practice the equality of self and others, And practice the exchange of self and others.
gm: Without despondency, and with the forces, Applying oneself earnestly, and mastering oneself, Equalizing self and other, And exchanging self and other, you should practice!

dm: One should not be discouraged, thinking, "How could I ever attain enlightenment?" For the Tathāgata, the Speaker of Truth, Has spoken this truth.
gm: Thinking, "How could I attain enlightenment?" I should not be despondent, For in this way the Tathāgata, Who speaks the truth, has spoken this truth:

dm: Even those who have become flies, gadflies, bees, Or likewise those who have become insects, If they develop the power of diligence, Will attain the supreme enlightenment so difficult to find.
gm: "Flies, mosquitoes, and bees, And likewise whatever is born as a worm, Even they, if they generate the power of effort, Will attain unsurpassable enlightenment, which is hard to find."

dm: Since I have been born as a human with the right potential, And recognize what is beneficial and what is harmful, If I do not abandon the conduct of a Bodhisattva, Why should I not attain enlightenment?
gm: Since someone like me is born as a human by birth, And recognizes what is beneficial and harmful, If I do not forsake the enlightenment conduct, Why should I not attain enlightenment?

dm: If you are afraid, thinking that you must give away Your limbs and so forth, It is merely the fear of a confused person Who has failed to analyze what is heavy and what is light.
gm: "But my arms, legs, and so forth, Must be given away, so I am afraid," if I think— Without examining what is heavy and what is light, Due to foolishness I am merely afraid.

dm: For countless tens of millions of eons, You have been cut, pierced, burned, and split apart many times over, Yet you have not attained enlightenment; And this will not lead to the attainment of enlightenment.
gm: For countless tens of millions of eons, I have been cut many times, Pierced, burned, and split apart, But did not attain enlightenment.

dm: The suffering I endure to achieve enlightenment is finite; It is like the pain of an incision made in the body To remove and destroy the harm of a deeply embedded splinter.
gm: The suffering of my accomplishing enlightenment Has a limit; To remove the harm of an internal thorn, It is like the suffering of making a cut in the body.

dm: All physicians use medical treatments To eliminate the discomfort of disease; Therefore, to destroy a multitude of sufferings, One should endure a minor discomfort.
gm: Even all doctors, through medical treatments, Cure illness with discomfort. Therefore, to destroy many sufferings, I should endure a minor discomfort.

dm: The Supreme Physician does not employ Common medical treatments such as these; Through extremely gentle procedures, He heals immeasurable and grievous illnesses.
gm: Such ordinary medical treatments Are not performed by the supreme physician; With an extremely gentle method, He cures immeasurable great diseases.

dm: The Guide first engages one in the giving of things such as vegetables; Once accustomed to that, one later gradually gives even one's own flesh.
gm: Even in the giving of vegetables and so forth, The Guide initially engages one. Having become accustomed to that, later on, One will gradually give away even one's own flesh.

dm: When one has developed an attitude toward one's own body As being like vegetables and the like, Then what difficulty could there be In giving away one's flesh and so forth?
gm: When toward one's own body A mind arises that views it like vegetables and so forth, At that time, in giving away flesh and so forth, What difficulty is there in that?

dm: Because non-virtue is abandoned, there is no suffering; Because of wisdom, there is no unhappiness. In this way, it is through distorted conceptions And non-virtue that the mind and body are harmed.
gm: By abandoning misdeeds, there is no suffering; By being wise, there is no displeasure. Thus, wrong conceptualizations And misdeeds harm the mind and body.

dm: If the body is at ease through merit, And the mind is at ease through wisdom, Then even while remaining in samsara for the sake of others, Why would those with compassion ever be weary?
gm: Through merit, the body is at ease, And through wisdom, the mind is at ease. Even while remaining in cyclic existence for the sake of others, Why would the compassionate ones become weary?

dm: Because this, through the power of the awakening mind, Exhausts previous misdeeds And gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained as superior to the Hearers.
gm: Because through the power of this awakening mind Former misdeeds are exhausted, And because it gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained to be supreme over the Hearers.

dm: Therefore, having mounted the horse of the awakening mind, Which dispels all weariness and fatigue, As one proceeds from joy to joy, What person of intelligence would ever succumb to despondency?
gm: Therefore, riding the horse of the awakening mind, Which dispels all weariness and fatigue, Proceeding from happiness to happiness, Who with a knowing mind would fall into despair?

dm: To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, one's forces are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated by fearing suffering and contemplating its benefits.
gm: The forces to accomplish the benefit of sentient beings Are aspiration, firmness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering And contemplating its benefits.

dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.

dm: I must eliminate the immeasurable faults of both myself and others; Since for each and every one of these faults, It would take an ocean of eons to exhaust them.
gm: The faults of myself and others, Being immeasurable, I must destroy; Wherein for even each single fault, An ocean of eons will be exhausted.

dm: If I do not perceive in myself even a fraction of the effort Needed to begin exhausting these faults, Then as a vessel of immeasurable suffering, Why does my heart not burst?
gm: Of that initiation of exhausting faults, If I do not see even a fraction in myself, Being an abode of immeasurable suffering, Why does my heart not burst?

dm: I must accomplish many virtues for both myself and others; Yet if even for a single virtue, One must train for an ocean of eons,
gm: The good qualities of myself and others, Being many, I must accomplish; Wherein if for even each single quality One must familiarize for an ocean of eons,

dm: I have never developed the habit of practicing even a fraction of such virtues. It is astonishing that I have rendered this birth, Which was somehow obtained, so meaningless.
gm: I, for even a fraction of a good quality, Have never generated familiarization; Having somehow found this birth, It is astonishing that I have made it meaningless.

dm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed One, Nor have I provided the joy of great festivals; I have not performed service for the Teachings, Nor have I fulfilled the hopes of the poor.
gm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed Ones, I have not provided the happiness of great festivals, I have not performed deeds for the teaching, I have not fulfilled the wishes of the poor.

dm: I have not granted fearlessness to the frightened, Nor have I given comfort to the distressed; I have merely produced the pain and suffering Of the womb of my mother.
gm: Not having given fearlessness to the fearful, And not having given happiness to the afflicted, I have merely produced the pangs And suffering of my mother's womb.
